# SK3041 — The compound operation on a `volatile` field is not atomic

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

`++`, `--` or a compound assignment is applied to a `volatile` field, which is a read and a write and not one operation.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Async |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 1.3 |
| ReSharper | `NonAtomicCompoundOperator` (`resharper_non_atomic_compound_operator_highlighting`) |

## Why

`volatile` buys visibility and orders nothing else. The read and the write of `counter++` are still two instructions with a window between them, so two threads read the same value and one update is lost — exactly as they would without the keyword. What makes this worth a warning rather than a hint is the keyword itself: it is the mark of an author who thought about threading and concluded wrongly, so the next reader trusts the field and does not look again.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
sealed class Counter {
    volatile int served;

    public void Serve() {
        served++;
    }
}
```

Write:

```csharp
sealed class Counter {
    int served;

    public void Serve() {
        Interlocked.Increment(ref served);
    }

    public int Served => Volatile.Read(ref served);
}
```

## When it does not fire

⚠ **Fixless, and the issue proposing it asked for a fix.** Four separate obstacles, each of which alone is enough: (1) `Interlocked.Increment(ref field)` on a `volatile` field is **CS0420** — a `ref` to a volatile field is not treated as volatile — so the obvious edit puts a compiler warning into code that had none; (2) `f++` as an *expression* yields the value before the increment and `Interlocked.Increment` yields the value after, so only the expression-statement position is rewritable at all; (3) `|=`, `&=` have an `Interlocked` form only on recent frameworks, `^=` has none, and `*=`, `/=`, `<<=` have none anywhere; (4) the honest repair — drop `volatile` and route every access through `Interlocked`/`Volatile` — changes the field's contract and touches every other access to it, including accesses in other files. `hasFix: false` states that rather than guessing. ⚠ **The rule withdraws inside a `lock`.** `volatile` beside a monitor is redundant, not wrong, and the update under the monitor is atomic; a finding there would send a reader to threading code that is correct. ⚠ **It withdraws in a constructor**, where no other thread can hold a reference to the instance yet — but *not* through a lambda written in one, because a delegate runs whenever somebody invokes it. ⚠ **Stated scope limit:** `Monitor.Enter` and a semaphore held across the statement are the same guarantee spelled without the keyword and are not recognised, so a field updated under one of those is reported. Deciding that the matching release runs on every path is a dataflow question this rule does not ask; the miss is a false positive rather than a silence, and the negative fixture set records it. `volatile` cannot be applied to `long`, `double` or `decimal`, so the widest-window cases of this bug cannot carry the keyword and are outside the rule by construction.
